title: Classify brace expansion and cd-opaque targets as unresolvable; globs stay untouched
judge_obligation_ack: standard lane: feature-close independent review pass covers the judge read

truths: A write-verb target carrying comma-or-range brace expansion (sta{t,t}e.json, f{1..9}.txt) denies on the Bash surface with a resolution-failure message naming brace expansion
A compound Bash command containing cd denies subsequent write-verb targets with a message naming the cd opacity (targets before the cd keep current behavior)
Plain glob characters (* ? [) are NOT classified — an rm *.log style command behaves exactly as before; no previously-denied command becomes allowed

action: Per CONTEXT.md D4: extend the Bash-surface classification (grw-2 landed it in the main.rs Bash branch) with two new unresolvable classes: (a) brace expansion — a target token containing an unquoted brace group with a comma or .. range; (b) cd opacity — when a compound command contains a cd segment, write-verb targets in LATER segments are unresolvable because the guard cwd no longer matches the shell cwd. Each class gets its own message sentence. Globs are explicitly out (record that in the code comment). Red-first tests: both new classes deny with their wording; rm *.log unchanged; targets before a cd unchanged; fail-closed only.
acceptance: All three must_haves truths hold with named tests; suite green
